title: Per-batch cost & latency snapshot - Arjun's scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick per-batch snapshot to compare small experiment runs across model variants and caching settings. Personal scratchpad — don’t treat as canonical.

Measurement notes:
- Single GPU (A100-sim) local cluster; microbench harness v0.9 (script: bench/quick_batch.sh).
- Each row = median of 5 runs, 30s steady-state after warmup.
- Cost estimated from per-GPU-second unit cost (0.48 USD / GPU-hour) translated to per-token using tokens/sec. crude but consistent.
- p95 measured via harness percentile collector; jitter due to host background IO.

Table (CSV-style):
date,model,variant,batch_size,avg_latency_ms,p95_latency_ms,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1k_tokens_usd,kv_cache,notes
2025-02-10,redwood-7b,cpu-fp16,1,48,92,210,0.0023,disabled,baseline single-request
2025-02-10,redwood-7b,cpu-fp16,8,110,220,610,0.0011,disabled,batching helps but latency jump for first token
2025-02-13,redwood-7b,quant-8bit,8,90,180,720,0.0009,disabled,quantized improved throughput by ~18%
2025-02-15,redwood-7b,quant-8bit,8,65,120,980,0.0007,enabled,kv-cache warmed on prefixes -> big p95 win
2025-02-18,redwood-70b,amp-x64,1,320,520,120,0.0080,disabled,large model single-shot
2025-02-18,redwood-70b,amp-x64,4,990,1800,320,0.0030,disabled,batched high variance
2025-02-20,redwood-70b,quant-4bit,4,720,1200,420,0.0023,enabled,quant+kv gives best cost/throughput seen so far

Quick observations:
- kv_cache on small-medium prompts reduces p95 a lot when traffic has repeated prefixes (see 02-15 row). Need to measure warmup hit rate for real traffic.
- Quantization gives consistent tokens/sec gains for 7B; diminishing returns for 70B due to memory-bound ops.
- Batch size sweet spot depends on model: 7B ~8, 70B ~4 for our hardware. Confirm on dedicated cluster.
- Cost calc is naive: excludes infra overhead (io, router), but ok for relative comparisons.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups (notes to self):
- Re-run 70B quant-4bit with with/without KV across different prefix similarity distributions (synthetic): LIN-1212 created for tracking.
- Add per-request cold-start latency column (first-token cost) in next snapshot.
- Cross-compare with dedicated pool config (dedicated-1) — schedule on Wed with SRE.
- Instrument per-batch memory-residency (GPU mem spill events) to explain p95 spikes.

Quick todo (priority order):
- [ ] Add cold-start column and re-run 7B rows (target: 2025-03-03)
- [ ] Attach harness logs + flame graphs to PR #4321
- [ ] Draft short note for console-team: suggestion to expose kv-hit-rate in route metrics (small email).

Slack / refs: see slack thread (serving-runtime) with sample trace: slack:#serving-runtime/thread/1690000000. Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4321

Random scribbles: burst policy may be interacting badly with batching window (50ms) -> consider dynamic window tuned by incoming rps. Also worth trying continuous batching with kv-aware eviction.

End of snapshot.
